deep.reconstruction: Setting, continuing from the previous pages. X is a space with a two-step stratification: a closed stratum Y and an open stratum X* = X \ Y. U*_{Y,X} is the deleted tubular neighbourhood, i.e. the 'link' or homotopy link of Y in X. It comes with a projection p: U* → Y and an inclusion j: U* → X*. The 'systems (17)' are presumably gluing data: local systems on Y and on X*, plus a comparison on the link. They form a topos F. Applying π_1 gives a span of fundamental groupoids B = π_1(Y) ← A = π_1(U*) → C = π_1(X*). Grothendieck builds a single category, which I call 𝒞. Its objects are the disjoint union of the objects of A, B and C. Its arrows are those of the three groupoids, plus arrows from an object a of A to an object b of B, defined as arrows p_*(a) → b in B. Likewise, arrows a → c to an object c of C are arrows j_*(a) → c in C. In modern terms 𝒞 is the collage (cograph, or Grothendieck construction) of the span of groupoids. His claim (22) is F ≃ 𝒞^ (presheaves on 𝒞, up to variance). It follows that the homotopy type of the topos F is the nerve of 𝒞. That nerve is the homotopy pushout (double mapping cylinder) BB ⊔^h_{BA} BC, which recovers the homotopy type of X. Example: X = ℂ, Y = {0}. Here A = π_1(D_0*) ≅ ℤ (a disc around 0 with 0 removed), B is trivial, and C = π_1(ℂ*) ≅ ℤ with A → C an isomorphism. The homotopy pushout is contractible, matching the fact that ℂ is topologically trivial. The next page recasts this through a category with a final object. That page then contrasts the case X = ℙ^1 with Y = {∞}, where the amalgamated sum is S^2. The purpose is to show that the topos of stratified local-system data has the homotopy type of the underlying stratified space. The previous page notes that products of the model D* → D, ℂ* give the local models for normal-crossings divisors.
errors: Minor imprecision. With three groupoids A, B, C, the category 𝒞 for X = ℂ does not literally have a final object: there are Hom(j_*a, c) ≅ ℤ arrows a → c and nothing from c back. The next page's 'b is final' description seems to use a simplified two-object version, or one where C is identified with A because A → C is an equivalence. Either way the homotopy conclusion (contractibility) is correct, since pt ⊔^h_{Bℤ} Bℤ ≃ pt.
The variance (presheaves on 𝒞 versus functors on 𝒞, i.e. exit versus entrance paths) is not specified on this page.
The object set is transcribed as '{0,3}'. This is probably a misreading, e.g. of Ob A ⊔ Ob B ⊔ Ob C, or of {a,b}.

ideas.what: The category of gluing data (local systems on the strata plus link data) is equivalent to presheaves on a category assembled from the fundamental groupoids of the strata and of the link.
ideas.modern_name: Exit-path category / constructible sheaves ≃ representations of the exit-path category
ideas.usually_credited_to: MacPherson (unpublished, 1990s); Treumann (2009); Lurie, Higher Algebra App. A; Ayala–Francis–Tanaka
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) alludes to dévissage of stratified structures and tubular neighbourhoods, but without this explicit formula.

ideas.what: Collage (cograph) of a span of groupoids B ← A → C, with arrows a → b given by Hom_B(p_*a, b).
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard category theory (Grothendieck construction, SGA1/SGA4); collages as in Street and others
ideas.where_published: SGA1 / SGA4 (fibred categories), as a general tool

ideas.what: The homotopy type of the topos 𝒞^ equals the nerve of 𝒞, which is the homotopy pushout of the classifying spaces; this recovers X (contractible for ℂ, S^2 for ℙ^1).
ideas.modern_name: Homotopy pushout along the homotopy link; Quillen Theorem A / Thomason-type colimit

ideas.what: Products of the model D* ⊂ D, ℂ* give the local models of normal-crossings stratifications.
ideas.modern_name: Local models for normal crossings / log geometry (Kato–Nakayama spaces)

missed.claim: Around 1981 Grothendieck describes the topos of stratified local-system data as presheaves on a collage of the fundamental groupoids of the strata and the link. This is in effect an exit-path category for two-step stratifications, and he checks that its homotopy type is that of X. This predates MacPherson's and Treumann's exit-path formalism.
missed.quote: les flèches d'un objet a de A = π_1 U*_{Y,X} vers un objet soit de B ..., soit de C = π_1 X*, définies comme étant les flèches p_*(a) → b dans B (resp. j_*(a) → c dans C)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority for the 'stratified homotopy hypothesis' and the exit-path description of constructible sheaves, attributed today to MacPherson, Treumann, Lurie and Ayala–Francis–Tanaka. It is folklore-level mathematically but undocumented as Grothendieck's.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is now standard: collage of groupoids, exit paths, homotopy pushout. Its explicit appearance in Grothendieck's 1981 notes, tied to the topos of a stratified space and to normal-crossings models, is a notable unpublished anticipation, but not a new result.
transcription_corrections: 'son type d'homotopie est connexe[?] décrit par celui du type 𝔉' should probably read '...est aussi décrit par celui du topos 𝔉 des systèmes (17)'.
'{0,3}' is likely a misreading; the object set is the union of the objects of the three groupoids, perhaps written as Ob A ⊔ Ob B ⊔ Ob C.
The inserted line reads approximately 'où dans le diagramme D ⇒ π_1(U*_{Y,X}) ⇉ π_1(X*, x_0)'; this is diagram (19) on π_1, with π_1(Y) = {1} crossed out.
'B = π_1 Y*_X' should be B = π_1(Y) (the struck-through ✱ is a correction).
'et dans les flèches sont, en plus de 18)' is likely 'et dont les flèches sont, en plus des flèches de ces trois groupoïdes'; the duplicated line is a transcription artifact.
